statement: The graphical interface shall allow researchers to use the transformation system without using the command line or low-level service calls.
The graphical interface shall make it faster to set up a transformation.
The graphical interface shall support running proven transformations on abstract programs.
The graphical interface shall present transformation results clearly enough to support experimentation and iteration.
Researchers working on high-assurance software transformations shall be able to create transformation requests.
Some users shall have read-only access to review results.
Administrators or technical maintainers shall be able to manage the platform setup.
Administrators or technical maintainers shall possibly be able to manage access control.
A transformation shall be runnable only if the input program and transformation configuration are complete and valid.
A transformation shall be runnable only if the transformation being used is one of the proven approved transformations available in the system.
The GUI shall support importing or selecting the abstract program to be transformed.
The GUI shall support related artifacts needed to understand or reproduce the transformation run.
The related artifacts shall include transformation metadata.
The related artifacts shall include configuration files.
The workflow shall require the user to fill in only the parameters that the selected transformation requires.
The system shall verify that the selected program is in a supported abstract form.
The system shall confirm that the configuration matches the selected transformation version before allowing execution.

The interface shall let a user take a prepared application and invoke the transformation without interacting with the underlying services directly.
The interface shall preserve enough provenance information for the user to trust which transformation was applied and under what inputs.
The system shall show users a simple running state during a transformation.
The system shall show a short error message when an error occurs.
The system should provide additional detail about the current stage for longer transformations when possible.
The system should avoid making the status detail too technical.
The system shall allow users to compare the transformed program against the input.
If annotations or metadata explain why the transformation is considered proven or semantics-preserving, the system should show them alongside the result.
The interface shall make it easier for researchers to try out transformations without having to deal with the underlying command-line services every time.
The interface shall support more accessible experimentation with semantics-preserving transformations.
The interface shall allow users to prepare inputs.
The interface shall allow users to run proven transformations.
The interface shall allow users to inspect results with confidence.
The actual transformation work shall occur in the existing High Assurance Transformation System services, not inside the GUI.
The GUI shall be used by researchers and authorized developers in a controlled environment.
The GUI shall be platform-independent and reasonably easy to deploy.
The system shall support preparing the application before transformation submission.

The system shall wait for the transformation service to complete after submission.
The system shall allow a reviewer to inspect the output after the transformation completes.

The system shall allow users to load or enter a program.

The first release shall exclude advanced search and filtering features.
The first release shall exclude detailed audit trails.
The first release shall exclude collaboration controls.
The first release shall exclude experiment templates.
The first release shall exclude repository management features that are not part of core transformation review.
The first release shall provide a reliable interface for preparing transformations.
The system shall support users in evaluating whether a transformation preserves the intended semantics of the program.
The system shall not require users to spend time on command-line invocation mechanics.
The current process shall fit reliably at submission.
The system shall avoid failures or ambiguities at submission, execution, and result inspection because they interrupt analysis.
For a transformation that is part of a normal exploratory run and whose output looks consistent, the system should prioritize speed over deeper inspection.
If the program is unusual, the transformation is complex, or the result differs in a surprising way, the system should support deeper inspection before users trust the result.
The system should provide extra caution when a run fails.
The system should provide extra caution when the input is large.
The system should provide extra caution when the input is sensitive.

The goal should be recorded as tentative for the moment.
The wording of the goal should be confirmed with the researchers before it is locked in as a formal goal.
Users are trying to preserve the semantics of the original program.
Users are trying to judge whether the transformed result is trustworthy for further analysis or reuse.
The wording for the transformed result should be confirmed as either “trustworthy,” “semantically equivalent,” or “behavior-preserving.”
Researchers usually refer to the original program as the source program or input program.
Researchers describe acceptable changes as semantics-preserving transformations or, depending on the case, refinement.
Researchers judge the result by whether the transformed program is equivalent in the relevant sense and still suitable for downstream analysis.
Researchers judge the result by whether the transformed program is still suitable for verification.
Researchers judge the result by whether the transformed program is still suitable for reuse.
The system shall leave wording choices flexible for researchers to standardize later.

Any system-defined terms that must be preserved exactly shall be verified separately.
Access to the underlying transformation services may need to be restricted depending on the environment.

There is no mandatory interface technology stack to impose for the first release.

The team should confirm whether they have a strong preference for a particular framework.
The system should support the common cases first.

Most advanced workflow features should be excluded from the first release unless they are needed to support basic research use.
Sharing should be treated as a later enhancement unless the team identifies it as essential for the initial experiment-and-inspect workflow.
Templates should be treated as a later enhancement unless the team identifies it as essential for the initial experiment-and-inspect workflow.
Search should be treated as a later enhancement unless the team identifies it as essential for the initial experiment-and-inspect workflow.

The interface shall be updated when new transformation types are added.
The interface shall be updated when new parameters are added.
The interface shall be updated when new result views are added.
The interface shall be updated when the underlying service contract changes.
Updates shall preserve existing workflows and shall not break researchers' saved applications or their ability to inspect prior results.
If an incompatible change is required, the system shall provide a clear migration path and advance notice so users are not interrupted unexpectedly.
The system shall anticipate irregular update timing rather than a fixed release schedule.
The interface shall be adaptable to occasional changes.
The owner should fix defects in the GUI.
The owner should adjust the GUI for new capabilities.

The system shall handle the transformation application as a core data object.
The system shall handle the abstract program or input being transformed as a core data object.
The system shall handle the resulting transformed output as a core data object.
The system shall allow researchers to keep track of the transformation settings or parameters they used.
The system shall support reproduction or comparison of runs later using the tracked transformation settings or parameters.
The system shall treat intermediate results or proof-related artifacts, if exposed, as part of the same workflow rather than as separate business objects.
The system shall catch submission issues up front and display a helpful message before any processing runs.
The system shall report transformation failures as system or service errors during execution.
The system shall show problems with the resulting program as a result-quality or validation issue after the transformation completes.
The system shall help researchers determine whether they need to fix their input, retry the service, or inspect the output more closely.
The system shall capture all settings needed to reproduce a run.
The system shall capture the chosen transformation as part of the settings.
The system shall capture any options or flags as part of the settings.
The system shall capture the input program reference as part of the settings.
The system shall capture any proof or validation preferences as part of the settings.
The system shall allow default settings to be inherited when a researcher starts a new run.
The system shall clearly mark any setting changed for one experiment as overridden.
The system shall prevent overridden settings from silently affecting later runs.
The system shall treat a setting that depends on a specific program or transformation instance as single-run only unless the team has explicitly defined it as reusable.
Overridden values should stay attached to the run only by default.
A researcher who wants to reuse overridden values should be able to do so via an explicit save or "make template" action.
The system should not carry overridden values forward automatically, because automatic carryover could create confusion about whether later runs are still using the original approved configuration.
The current run shall keep its exact configuration as the record of what actually happened.
The reusable copy shall be a separate editable object.
The reusable version shall be versioned so researchers can see how it evolved.
The reusable version shall be linked back to the approved run or the run it came from for traceability.

The system shall allow a researcher to select a proven transformation when the goal is to apply a trusted, semantics-preserving transformation to an eligible abstract program and the system has enough information to validate that fit.
The GUI shall prevent or warn against selecting a proven transformation when the input or requested options fall outside what the proven transformation supports.
The proven transformation option shall be available only when it maintains confidence in the result and matches the researcher’s intent.
The GUI should be web-based first to maintain platform independence and avoid installation for researchers.
A desktop client should be considered later if the team needs tighter integration with local files, offline work, or a controlled lab environment.
If the transformation services are only reachable inside a secure network, the system should carefully consider authentication and deployment location.
For the first release, the system should use the web GUI only unless there is a strong need for local file workflows that cannot be handled through upload and download.
For the first release, the system should use the web GUI only unless researchers must work offline.
If the main use case is a restricted lab network, the web interface should be deployed inside that environment.
If the main use case is a restricted lab network, the web interface should support straightforward authentication.
The system should add a desktop option only if users genuinely need access to local resources or disconnected work that the web application cannot support cleanly.
The interface should react almost immediately, even if the full transformed view takes longer to render.
If rendering takes more than a couple of seconds, the interface should show progress or a partial view rather than leaving the user wondering whether it is frozen.
For very large programs, the system should defer some details until they are requested.
The system shall start a run only when the researcher explicitly confirms it.
The system shall allow the researcher to explicitly confirm a run by clicking a clearly labeled "Run Transformation" or "Execute" action.
The system shall support confirming the run on a review screen, if a review screen is provided, so the researcher can see the chosen inputs before execution.
The GUI should let researchers choose a proven transformation only when the input program matches the transformation’s proven scope and the requested options stay within the documented constraints.
If only part of the program is outside the proven scope, the GUI shall clearly flag this before the run and shall not present the transformation as fully proven.
If only part of the program is outside the proven scope, the user shall either adjust the input or select a different transformation that is fully applicable.
If partial application is accepted in some cases, the system shall provide a very explicit warning and probably a separate mode, and treat this as an exception.

The system shall support a view that is easy to share with colleagues for review, if useful.

The system shall allow finalized outputs to be exported.
The system shall allow review snapshots to be exported.

If a user tries to export an ineligible state, the GUI shall stop the export and explain why it is blocked.

The export shall carry the run timestamp.

The system shall support tracing back to the originating input and run.

If a retry affected only a particular output region or transformation step, the UI should allow an optional combined view for a quick overall check.
If the recovery was effectively transparent and did not change any semantics or outputs, the system should allow a combined result view.
If the recovery was effectively transparent and did not change any semantics or outputs, the user should still be able to drill down to see the split.
The export shall include the run identifier.

Any field that affects traceability or reproducibility shall remain in the export.

The system should preserve backward compatibility as much as possible for comparisons.
